data.name: Rapture - World Conquest
data.detailed_description:
The End is coming! Bombard the globe with devastating miracles and decimate the enemy civilizations. Guide swarms of armies to dominate the planet and catch your people up to heaven!

Fast, frantic, global population annihilation!

====================

Now completely free - enjoy!

====================

Features
– Fast, simple RTS gameplay – squeezing 3000 years of civilization into a 5 minute blitz
– Play against 3 friends online or over a local network
– 12 devastating miracles to hurl down from above - Meteors, Earthquakes, Tsunamis, Volcanoes and others
– 38 civilizations to take control of and lead to victory
– Fast strategic action as you battle to control the largest number of regions before the end of times
– New civilizations, globe shapes, skies and atmospheres to unlock
– Dozens of achievements and missions to complete

====================

Rapture - World Conquest is a fast paced real-time 4x wargame that puts you in the celestial shoes of a jealous god. Guide your followers through the ages and vanquish the unbelievers in the surrounding kingdoms. Send your armies to take over regions and expand your realm.

As your followers rise in numbers their adulation will provide mana allowing you to unleash devastating miracles – lightning storms, hurricanes, floods and other death from above. Conquer the globe and as the supreme deity you will lift your people up to heaven and leave your remaining enemies to the apocalypse.

Domination is your ultimate goal. Should you risk all on military warfare? On science and technical achievements? Or improve farming to boost productivity? Or perhaps your followers should spend their time praising you, giving you the power to unleash more miracles.

Inspired by classic god games such as Civ and Populous, reinvented for short match times on mobile. There are dozens of missions, achievements and unlockable content.

You are a jealous god, wipe out the minions of your rivals, conquer the world and rapture your people.

====================

We hope you enjoy playing Rapture – World Conquest! We are keen to hear your ideas for new features! Please get in touch.

Follow us on Facebook and Twitter and let us know what you think.

reviews.review:
Rapture - World Conquest is a remarkably fast interpretation of the civilization strategy formula, turning the rise and fall of entire societies into matches that can be completed in only a few minutes. Developed and published by Tundra Games Ltd, it puts the player in the position of a deity guiding a civilization toward global dominance. Rather than dealing with hours of city management, diplomacy, and economic planning, the game concentrates on expansion, technological development, warfare, worship, and spectacular divine intervention. The result is a lightweight strategy experience that feels closer to an arcade-style god game than a traditional grand strategy title.

The pace is immediately noticeable because thousands of years of history are compressed into roughly five-minute matches. There is little room for hesitation. Territories need to be captured, neighboring civilizations must be watched carefully, and development priorities can quickly determine whether an empire expands or disappears. This condensed format gives the game an identity of its own. Familiar civilization-building ideas are present, but almost everything has been simplified so that the player spends more time making immediate decisions than studying complicated menus.

Civilization development revolves around several important priorities. Military investment helps with aggressive expansion, while science and technology improve the civilization in other ways. Farming contributes to growth and productivity, and religion is especially important because followers generate mana through worship. This divine resource connects the civilization-management side of the game with its most entertaining feature: supernatural powers. Choosing where to focus development becomes a balancing act, particularly because the rapid pace makes it difficult to maximize everything simultaneously.

The selection of miracles adds considerable personality to each match. The player can unleash devastating events such as earthquakes, meteors, hurricanes, floods, lightning, volcanoes, and tsunamis. These abilities are not merely visual effects because using them at the right moment can disrupt an opponent's expansion or completely change the territorial situation. There is a satisfying contrast between gradually strengthening a civilization and suddenly intervening as an all-powerful deity. It helps separate the experience from more conventional territory-conquest games.

Replayability comes from the variety of civilizations and unlockable content. There are 38 civilizations to encounter, alongside different globe configurations, atmospheric appearances, and skies. Missions and achievements provide additional goals beyond simply conquering the world. Because individual sessions are so short, unlocking new options works well as a reason to keep playing. Losing is also less frustrating than it would be in a lengthy strategy campaign because another attempt requires only a modest investment of time.

Multiplayer further complements this design, allowing competition with up to three friends. Short matches are particularly suitable for multiplayer because participants are not committing themselves to the lengthy sessions commonly associated with strategy games. Competitive players can also pursue leaderboard performance, while achievements and trading cards provide additional Steam-related incentives. The overall feature set is surprisingly broad considering how deliberately compact the core gameplay is.

Visually, the game favors clarity and simplicity over elaborate spectacle. Viewing the action across a globe reinforces the fantasy of being a deity observing civilizations from above. Territorial expansion remains easy to understand even while the world changes rapidly, and the various disasters provide some welcome visual excitement. The presentation is certainly modest compared with larger strategy productions, but it serves the quick gameplay effectively and contributes to the game's relatively accessible hardware requirements.

The biggest weakness is the unavoidable consequence of its greatest strength. By compressing civilization strategy into extremely short sessions, much of the depth associated with the genre disappears. Players expecting sophisticated diplomacy, detailed economies, extensive city construction, complex military organization, or enormous technology trees will probably find the systems shallow. Strategic choices still matter, but they operate on a much smaller scale. There simply is not enough time for elaborate long-term plans to develop in the same way they would during a traditional 4X campaign.

However, judging the game entirely by those standards would miss its purpose. It is better approached as a rapid strategy game inspired by civilization builders and classic god games. Its appeal comes from watching borders change quickly, developing followers, generating divine power, and deciding when a catastrophic miracle will have the greatest effect. There is a certain charm to seeing thousands of years of fictional history unfold at an absurd speed, especially when a seemingly dominant opponent can suddenly become vulnerable.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially categorized as Playable rather than fully Verified. Performance with the default graphics configuration is considered suitable, and the game can run successfully on SteamOS. However, handheld players should expect compromises. Some functionality is not fully accessible through the default controller configuration, touchscreen interaction or a community controller layout may occasionally be useful, and text entry can require manually opening the virtual keyboard. Some interface text may also appear small, while certain prompts can display keyboard, mouse, or non-Steam Deck controller icons. It is therefore functional on the Deck, but the experience is less seamless than a fully optimized handheld release.

Rapture - World Conquest ultimately delivers an enjoyable miniature version of global conquest. Its short matches, accessible mechanics, numerous civilizations, destructive miracles, progression elements, and multiplayer support make it easy to play repeatedly without requiring a major time commitment. It lacks the strategic richness of more ambitious civilization games, but that is largely intentional. For players interested in quick territorial strategy with a humorous dose of divine destruction, it offers an unusual and entertaining experience.

Rating: 7/10

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows XP SP3, Vista, Windows 7 or later
  • Processador: 1.4Ghz Dual Core or better
  • Memória: 1 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: DirectX 9.0c compliant video card (Shader Model 3.0) with 256MB VRAM
  • DirectX: Versão 9.0c
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 300 MB de espaço livre

mac_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo: OS X version 10.8 (Mountain Lion) or later
  • Processador: 1.6 Ghz Intel Core 2 Duo or better
  • Memória: 2 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: GeForce 9400M with 256 MB RAM or better
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 300 MB de espaço livre
